references.text: Moses performs the consecration of Aaron and his sons with the second ram, called the ram of consecration, where they lay their hands on the ram's head.
The same laying-on-of-hands ritual is performed earlier in the chapter with the first ram as a sin offering.
Laying hands on the head of the sacrificial animal is a fundamental element of the sacrifice ritual, symbolizing identification with the offering.
For the peace offering, the one sacrificing must lay their hand on the animal's head before slaughter.
Laying hands on the head of the sacrificial animal is required for the sin offering.
This second ram is called the ram of consecration, and its meat is to be eaten by Aaron and his sons.
The book of Hebrews explains how Christ as high priest surpasses the Levitical priests who had to be consecrated through repeated sacrifices.
Thematic parallel: The same consecration ritual, but describing an earlier offering (the burnt offering) with identical laying on of hands.
Structural parallel: First step in the same ritual (the sin offering bull) with identical laying on of hands as preparation for the rams.
Ritual parallel: Laying on of hands on the sin offering bull as part of the same consecration process as the rams.
